Theme

Latin word

cautiō

cautiō, cautiōnis f.

noun, third declension

caution, care; a written guarantee, a bond; insurance; a bond, a written guarantee (in law)

In this lexicon

  • cautious

    also used · classical · Traupman 150; Lewis & Short: “wariness, precaution, caution”; Traupman 288

  • guarantee

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.18.1: Graeculam tibi mīsī cautiōnem chīrographī meī

  • insurance

    the recommended word · modern · Traupman 333: prō vītā cautiō, life insurance; M-O s.v. insurance: life insurance, vītae cautiō (after Egger); Traupman 333

  • security

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.18.1: Graeculam tibi mīsī cautiōnem chīrographī meī (Lewis & Short)

Notes

  1. 1Lewis & Short gives cautiō as “an obligation, security, bond, warranty, bail”; its use for a maker’s or seller’s guarantee on goods is ours.

Examples

  • quoniam vestrae cautiōnēs īnfirmae sunt, Graeculam tibi mīsī cautiōnem chīrographī meī

    since you lawyers’ guarantees are worth so little, I have sent you a little Greek guarantee in my own handCic. Fam. 7.18.1
